sections.h2: Where is Savage, Minnesota, and how did it get its name?
sections.html:
Savage lies in Scott County on the Minnesota River's south bank, some 15 miles south-southwest of downtown Minneapolis. The river forms its northern boundary, and the Credit River runs north through the city to meet it. The Census Bureau lists 15.61 square miles of land.

Traders set up a post where the Credit and Minnesota rivers meet in 1852. Irish and Scottish settlers built a landing named Hamilton, and the town was incorporated in 1892 as the village of Hamilton. In 1902 a Minneapolis businessman, Marion Willis Savage, bought the racing horse Dan Patch and trained him at a farm inside the village limits. The town was renamed for him in 1904, and in 1906 Dan Patch set a world pacing mile record at the Minnesota State Fair.

During World War II the city housed Camp Savage, a military intelligence language school, and Cargill built Navy ships at Port Cargill on the river. Roughly 17 blocks of the late 19th century town still make up downtown along Highway 13.

sections.h2: How fast has Savage grown, and what do its housing numbers look like?
sections.html:
Savage stayed small for decades because the river cut it off and no interstate reached it. Upgrades to Highway 13 in the 1980s and the Bloomington Ferry Bridge in 1996 changed that, and the Census Bureau counted 26,911 people in 2010 and 32,465 in 2020. The July 1, 2025 estimate is 32,970, a 1.6 percent rise over the 2020 base of 32,463.

Roughly 93 percent of residents stayed in the same house for the previous year. With households averaging 2.74 people and a quarter of residents under 18, Savage skews toward families.

sections.h2: Which roads, schools and open land shape a Savage sale?
sections.html:
Highway 13 and County Road 42 carry most traffic across Savage, while I-35W and U.S. 169 pass just outside its borders. Savage still has undeveloped land, including parts of the Minnesota Valley National Wildlife Refuge and the Murphy-Hanrehan Park Reserve.

Three school districts serve Savage, which is easy to overlook when you describe a house:

  • Prior Lake-Savage District 719, with Redtail Ridge, Hamilton Ridge and Glendale elementary schools feeding Prior Lake High School.
  • Burnsville-Eagan-Savage District 191, with Harriet Bishop and Hidden Valley elementaries and Eagle Ridge Middle School feeding Burnsville High School.
  • Shakopee District 720.

Buyers ask which district covers an address, so confirm it before listing. The Census Bureau's 2022 figures show about $399.3 million in retail sales and $94.7 million in health care receipts in the city.

sections.h2: Is Savage rental registration mandatory, and does it cost anything?
sections.html:
Registration is mandatory and free. Savage's residential rental ordinance, Title 11, Chapter 121, requires owners to register with the city so emergency services and the city have a contact for each rental. The city describes the ordinance as a partnership with owners and ties it to Crime Free Residential Rental Property training offered at several Minnesota locations.

An owner of a rental who plans to sell can do the following:

  • Read the registration ordinance before you fill out the form.
  • Ask the city how to close out or update your registration once the house is sold.
  • Pass the registration and training information to the buyer so they can register under their own name.

The city's property protection pages are the place to start with questions.

sections.h2: How do Scott County property taxes and appeals work for a Savage house?
sections.html:
Scott County's second-half 2026 installment fell due on Thursday, October 15, so no 2026 payment is outstanding on a current account. Owners pay through eNotices Online (a $1.50 charge for an e-check, 2.3 percent for a card), by mail, in a Government Center drop box, or at a county library box in the weeks before a deadline. Property and Taxation Services is at 952-496-8115.

Postal postmarks now show the day mail is first processed, not the day it was dropped off. The county suggests paying electronically, requesting a hand postmark, or mailing several business days early.

A Savage owner who thinks the value is high should bring evidence, such as an appraisal or recent comparable sales, to the city assessor. The next stop is the open book or local board session named on the value notice, and after it the county board of appeal. Tax Court is the final stage, with an April 30 filing cutoff.

sections.h2: What does the Scott County Land Records office do for a Savage seller?
sections.html:
The Scott County Land Records Department records deeds, mortgages, assignments, releases and satisfactions. Its number is 952-496-8150, and plats and priority documents such as sheriff foreclosures or certificates of redemption require an appointment. Electronic, mail and drop-box recordings are processed.

  • Property Watch is a free service that emails the owner when any document is recorded under their name and parcel number.
  • RecordEASE is the paid portal for searching documents by parcel, by document number, by plat or lien, or by tract index.
  • The office checks that a document is in recordable form but does not supply legal forms or advice, and it points people to the state's Uniform Conveyancing Blanks, an attorney or a title company.

Signing up for Property Watch is useful on the day you close, because you can see when the deed is recorded.

sections.h2: How does a sale change a Savage property's homestead status?
sections.html:
State law ties homestead status to the certificate of value. A sale above $3,000 requires one at the auditor's office when the deed is recorded, and without it the property cannot be classified as homestead (Minn. Stat. 272.115).

The assessor also removes the homestead classification for the next assessment year when a property is sold, unless the new owner completes a homestead application and qualifies. Scott County's Taxation page explains the homestead requirements and takes the application materials. That means a buyer who forgets the application can see a higher tax bill the following year, which is worth mentioning during negotiations.

sections.h2: What should I do first when a Savage house needs to sell quickly?
sections.html:
A short list of local checks saves time once you decide to move.

  • Find your parcel number on the Scott County property information site and print the current tax statement.
  • Confirm which of the three school districts covers the address.
  • Check whether a rental registration is on file with the city and whether any document is waiting to be recorded.
  • Ask a title company or attorney to prepare the deed on a Uniform Conveyancing Blank, since the county does not.

Most Savage homes are lived in by their owners, so many sales are plain family moves. A house with deferred repairs, a tenant or an estate history can still go to a buyer willing to take it in its present condition.

faqs.q: Does Savage charge to register a rental property?
faqs.a: No. The city says there is no charge for registering, but registration is mandatory under Title 11, Chapter 121 of the city code.

faqs.q: Which school district serves my Savage house?
faqs.a: It depends on the address, since Prior Lake-Savage District 719, Burnsville-Eagan-Savage District 191 and Shakopee District 720 all cover parts of the city. Contact the districts to confirm before you advertise.

faqs.q: How do I get alerts when a document is recorded on my Savage property?
faqs.a: Sign up for Scott County's Property Watch. It is free and needs only your name, property ID and email address, and it sends an alert when a document with your name and parcel number is recorded.

faqs.q: Can I still appeal my Scott County valuation this year?
faqs.a: The Minnesota Tax Court is the last step, with its cutoff on April 30 of the payable year. The meetings on your value notice come first, so read the notice each spring.

faqs.q: What does the Scott County Land Records office not do?
faqs.a: It does not provide legal forms, help completing them or legal advice. Staff refer people to an attorney or title company and to the state's Uniform Conveyancing Blanks.
